cls: Sodium-glucose co-transporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitor (oral antidiabetic / cardio-renal protective)
pharm: Inhibits renal SGLT2 in the proximal tubule, lowering the glucose reabsorption threshold and increasing urinary glucose excretion; also promotes natriuresis and osmotic diuresis, contributing to cardiovascular and renal benefit.
quick: 10 mg once daily in the morning; may increase to 25 mg
Take with or without food, in the morning
Not recommended for glycemic control if eGFR <30; contraindicated on dialysis
No dose adjustment; exposure rises with severity
Avoid excess; alcohol abuse predisposes to ketoacidosis
Renal function, volume status, ketones if acidosis suspected, glucose
summary: Empagliflozin (Jardiance) is an SGLT2 inhibitor that lowers blood glucose by increasing urinary glucose excretion and also reduces the risk of cardiovascular death and heart failure hospitalization. CRITICAL SAFETY: it can cause ketoacidosis (DKA) that may be EUGLYCEMIC - present even when blood glucose is less than 250 mg/dL - so any patient with metabolic acidosis must be assessed for ketoacidosis regardless of glucose; fatal cases have occurred. It also causes genital mycotic infections and rare but life-threatening necrotizing fasciitis of the perineum (Fournier's gangrene) in both sexes. Other key risks are volume depletion/hypotension, acute kidney injury, urosepsis/pyelonephritis, and hypoglycemia when combined with insulin or a sulfonylurea. Not for type 1 diabetes and contraindicated in patients on dialysis.
indications: To reduce the risk of cardiovascular death and hospitalization for heart failure in adults with heart failure
To reduce the risk of cardiovascular death in adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus and established cardiovascular disease
As an adjunct to diet and exercise to improve glycemic control in adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus

dosage.c: Type 2 diabetes / CV risk reduction / heart failure - initiation
dosage.t: In the morning, with or without food
dosage.n: Assess volume status and renal function and correct volume depletion before starting

dosage.d: May increase to 25 mg once daily

dosage.c: Glycemic control with eGFR <30 mL/min/1.73 m2
dosage.n: Likely ineffective for glucose lowering at this eGFR

dosage.d: Consider temporarily discontinuing for at least 3 days prior to surgery
dosage.n: Reduce ketoacidosis risk; resume after risk factors resolve

admin: Take 10 mg once daily in the morning, with or without food
Before initiating, assess volume status and renal function; correct volume depletion first
Educate patients on signs and symptoms of ketoacidosis and to seek care immediately if they occur
Hold therapy temporarily in situations predisposing to ketoacidosis (acute illness, prolonged fasting, surgery)
If combined with insulin or a sulfonylurea, consider lowering that agent's dose to reduce hypoglycemia
moa: Empagliflozin is a selective inhibitor of sodium-glucose co-transporter 2 (SGLT2), the predominant transporter responsible for reabsorbing filtered glucose in the proximal renal tubule. By inhibiting SGLT2, it lowers the renal threshold for glucose and increases urinary glucose excretion, reducing blood glucose independently of insulin. It also reduces sodium reabsorption and increases sodium delivery to the distal tubule, producing osmotic diuresis and natriuresis; these effects may lower cardiac pre- and afterload and downregulate sympathetic activity, contributing to its cardiovascular and renal benefits. Its glucose-lowering effect diminishes as eGFR falls.

absolute: Hypersensitivity to empagliflozin or any excipient (reactions such as angioedema have occurred)
relative: Type 1 diabetes mellitus (not indicated; increased ketoacidosis risk)
History or risk factors for diabetic ketoacidosis (pancreatic insulin deficiency, caloric restriction, alcohol abuse)
eGFR less than 30 mL/min/1.73 m2 for glycemic control (likely ineffective)
Volume depletion, hypotension, elderly, or concurrent loop diuretics (correct/assess before starting)
Recurrent genital mycotic or urinary tract infections
monitor: Renal function before and periodically during therapy
Ketones (blood/urine) if metabolic acidosis is suspected, regardless of glucose
Signs of genital/perineal infection (Fournier's gangrene) and urinary tract infection

preg: Not recommended during the second and third trimesters of pregnancy based on animal data showing adverse renal effects (renal pelvic and tubule dilatation). Available human data are insufficient to determine drug-associated risk; poorly controlled diabetes in pregnancy itself carries maternal and fetal risk. Advise patients of the potential fetal risk, especially in the second and third trimesters.
lact: There is limited information on the presence of empagliflozin in human milk; it is present in rat milk and may accumulate. Because human kidney maturation continues in utero and during the first 2 years of life, there may be risk to the developing kidney. Use of empagliflozin is not recommended while breastfeeding.
renal: Assess renal function before initiating and as clinically indicated. Not recommended for glycemic control when eGFR is less than 30 mL/min/1.73 m2 (likely ineffective). Contraindicated in patients on dialysis. Data are insufficient to recommend dosing in type 2 diabetes with established CVD and eGFR <30, or in heart failure with eGFR <20. SGLT2 inhibitors can cause acute kidney injury; impaired renal function increases volume-depletion risk.
hepatic: No dosage adjustment is required for hepatic impairment. Empagliflozin AUC increased by approximately 23%, 47%, and 75% in mild, moderate, and severe hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh), respectively; these increases are not considered clinically meaningful.

major: Insulin or insulin secretagogues (e.g., sulfonylureas) - increased hypoglycemia risk; consider lowering their dose
moderate: Diuretics (especially loop diuretics) - additive diuresis increases volume-depletion and hypotension risk; assess volume status before starting
Lithium - SGLT2 inhibitors may decrease serum lithium; monitor lithium levels more frequently on initiation and dose changes
minor: No clinically relevant CYP450 interactions; empagliflozin is a P-gp and BCRP substrate but does not inhibit them at therapeutic doses
interactions.food: May be taken with or without food; a high-fat meal slightly lowers exposure but not clinically relevant.
interactions.alcohol: Avoid excess alcohol; alcohol abuse is a predisposing factor for ketoacidosis.
interactions.diagnostics: Causes positive urine glucose tests and renders the 1,5-anhydroglucitol (1,5-AG) assay unreliable; do not use these to monitor glycemic control - use alternative methods.

serious: Ketoacidosis including euglycemic DKA (glucose may be <250 mg/dL)
rare: Necrotizing fasciitis of the perineum (Fournier's gangrene)
emergency: Diabetic ketoacidosis - assess for ketoacidosis in ANY patient with metabolic acidosis regardless of blood glucose (may be euglycemic, <250 mg/dL); fatal cases reported; discontinue and treat urgently
Fournier's gangrene - genital/perineal pain, erythema, swelling with fever/malaise; surgical emergency
Severe volume depletion / hypotension and acute kidney injury

monitoring: Renal function (eGFR) at baseline and periodically
Volume status, blood pressure, and signs of dehydration
Blood or urine ketones whenever metabolic acidosis is suspected, regardless of glucose level
Signs and symptoms of urinary tract infection, genital mycotic infection, and Fournier's gangrene
HbA1c and glucose (not via urine glucose or 1,5-AG)
counsel: Seek medical care immediately for nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, tiredness, or trouble breathing - these can signal ketoacidosis even when your blood sugar is not high
Report any pain, tenderness, redness, or swelling in the genital or perineal area with fever or feeling unwell - this can be a serious infection (Fournier's gangrene)
Genital yeast infections and urinary tract infections are common; report symptoms so they can be treated
Drink adequate fluids; stand up slowly as this medicine can lower blood pressure, especially with water pills
If you take insulin or a sulfonylurea, watch for low blood sugar and learn how to treat it
Hold this medicine and call your clinician if you are seriously ill, fasting, or before scheduled surgery
pk: Urinary glucose excretion increases immediately after the first dose
Peak plasma concentration about 1.5 hours post-dose
Glucosuric effect approaches baseline by about 3 days after stopping; dosed once daily
Store at controlled room temperature per labeling
pearls: DKA can be EUGLYCEMIC - assess for ketoacidosis in any patient on an SGLT2 inhibitor with metabolic acidosis regardless of blood glucose; fatal cases have occurred
Hold for at least 3 days before scheduled surgery and during acute illness, prolonged fasting, or dehydration to reduce ketoacidosis risk
Watch for genital mycotic infections and the rare but life-threatening Fournier's gangrene (necrotizing fasciitis of the perineum) in both men and women
Correct volume depletion and assess renal function before starting; risk is higher in the elderly, in renal impairment, and on loop diuretics
Lower the dose of concomitant insulin or sulfonylurea to limit hypoglycemia; empagliflozin alone rarely causes hypoglycemia
Causes positive urine glucose tests - use HbA1c/plasma glucose, not urine glucose or 1,5-AG, to monitor control
missed: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember that day. If it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and take the next one at the usual time. Do not take two doses at once.
overdose: In the event of overdose, contact the Poison Control Center and provide supportive care based on the patient's clinical status. Removal of empagliflozin by hemodialysis has not been studied. Monitor for volume depletion and, if metabolic acidosis develops, evaluate for ketoacidosis regardless of glucose.
